clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client arrives with fever, cough, conjunctivitis, and a new generalized maculopapular rash. The nurse suspects measles. Which infection-control response is most appropriate?

options.A: Place a facemask on the client, move the client to an airborne infection isolation room, and use a fit-tested N95 respirator for care.
options.B: Place the client in a private room with droplet precautions and use a surgical mask until laboratory confirmation is available.
options.C: Begin contact precautions with gown and gloves, keep the room door open, and add airborne precautions only if respiratory symptoms worsen.
options.D: Continue standard precautions in the current care area while specimens are collected, then isolate the client if measles testing is positive.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC measles infection-control guidance calls for rapid identification and isolation of clients with known or suspected measles and use of Standard and Airborne Precautions. CDC directs health care facilities to provide a facemask to a symptomatic client on arrival, place a known or suspected measles client in an airborne infection isolation room (AIIR), and have health care personnel use respiratory protection at least as protective as a fit-tested NIOSH-certified N95 respirator when entering the room or care area. Isolation should begin when measles is suspected rather than waiting for laboratory confirmation. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes understanding airborne transmission and applying isolation/transmission-based precautions under Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer; B uses the wrong transmission category, C does not provide appropriate airborne containment, and D delays indicated precautions.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For a client with suspected measles, initiate airborne infection-control measures promptly: mask the client for source control during placement, use an AIIR, and use appropriate N95-level respiratory protection for care.

scope_exclusions.laboratory_diagnosis: The item does not require laboratory confirmation before precautions. The tested action is infection-control response to a clinically suspected case.
scope_exclusions.isolation_duration: No number of days after rash onset or other isolation-duration rule is tested, avoiding unnecessary duration precision.
scope_exclusions.room_air_change_specifications: No air-changes-per-hour, room-clearance time or engineering threshold is asserted.
scope_exclusions.immunity_exception: The item does not use staff immunity as an exception to respiratory protection; current CDC measles guidance recommends N95-level respiratory protection for HCP entering the room or care area regardless of presumptive immunity status.
scope_exclusions.treatment: No antiviral, antibiotic, vitamin or postexposure prophylaxis regimen is tested.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for 'measles airborne isolation respirator' returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank rescan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It combines CDC-recommended source-control masking during placement, AIIR placement and N95-level respiratory protection for suspected measles.
option_audit.B: Plausible because droplet precautions apply to several respiratory infections, but measles requires Airborne Precautions rather than droplet-only precautions.
option_audit.C: Plausible because gown/glove use may be appropriate for other transmission routes, but contact precautions do not replace the airborne containment required for measles.
option_audit.D: Plausible diagnostic-waiting error, but CDC recommends immediate precautions for suspected measles rather than waiting for a positive test.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem explicitly presents suspected measles. A alone implements the CDC airborne response immediately; B uses the wrong transmission category, C fails airborne containment and D delays precautions pending testing.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. The correct option is not the longest; all four choices are parallel infection-control action sequences.
